ledgerSql:
select ledger.*, lot.coin_type as coin_type
          from platform_coin_ledger_entries as ledger
          left join platform_coin_lots as lot
            on lot.lot_ref = ledger.lot_ref
           and lot.wallet_ref = ledger.wallet_ref
         where ledger.wallet_ref = ?
           and (
             ? is null
             or ledger.occurred_at < ?
             or (ledger.occurred_at = ? and ledger.entry_ref < ?)
           )
         order by ledger.occurred_at desc, ledger.entry_ref desc
         limit ?

cases.title: key-changing UPDATE of a NOT-YET-READ row (miss boundary)

ops.sql: UPDATE platform_coin_ledger_entries SET occurred_at = '2026-03-06T12:00:00.000Z' WHERE entry_ref = 'le-pg-1030'

omissions.reason: production guard rejects ANY update of a ledger entry (unconditional RAISE coin_ledger_immutable); omitted in the experiment schema so the boundary can be documented

cases.note: le-pg-1030 sits on static page 3. Moving its occurred_at newer than the page-1 cursor moves it ahead of the reader, so it is never returned: exactly that row is MISSED. This is the mechanism boundary: keyset pagination cannot guarantee exactly-once if a sort key changes mid-traversal. Production guards make this write unreachable.

cases.title: key-changing UPDATE of an ALREADY-READ row (duplicate boundary)

ops.sql: UPDATE platform_coin_ledger_entries SET occurred_at = '2026-02-04T12:00:00.000Z' WHERE entry_ref = 'le-pg-1040'

omissions.reason: production guard rejects ANY update of a ledger entry (unconditional RAISE coin_ledger_immutable); omitted in the experiment schema so the boundary can be documented

cases.note: le-pg-1040 is read on page 1. Moving its occurred_at older than the page-1 cursor moves it behind the reader, so it is returned AGAIN on the tail page: exactly that row is DUPLICATED. Same boundary as L5. Production guards make this write unreachable.

cases.title: DELETE of a NOT-YET-READ row (absent boundary)

ops.sql: DELETE FROM platform_coin_ledger_entries WHERE entry_ref = 'le-pg-1020'

omissions.reason: production guard rejects ANY delete of a ledger entry (unconditional RAISE coin_ledger_immutable); omitted in the experiment schema so the boundary can be documented

cases.note: le-pg-1020 sits on static page 5. Deleting it after page 1 means it is never returned: it is ABSENT (recorded as missed-by-deletion, not as a pagination miss). Every other frozen row must appear exactly once. Production guards make this write unreachable; no FK references the ledger table, so nothing else blocks the delete in the experiment schema.
